solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vitamin taken orally, it's nearly agreed?

indicators.note: taken orally says the phrase is spoken, so its sound rather than its spelling gives the letters

parts.note: nearly is NIGH and agreed suggests ASSENT; said together, 'nigh assent' runs close to the vitamin's name

explanation.surface: A vitamin pill swallowed by mouth, with a query over whether everyone is more or less in agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken orally' fits a vitamin pill but it is the sound signal: 'nigh' (nearly) plus 'assent' (agreement) spoken quickly comes out like NY-a-sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Niacin is the B vitamin also called nicotinic acid, B3.

clue.text: Looking after one's own spot — and mine, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone guarding their own patch and mine, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking after' looks like caring, but the definition is favouring relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to relatives or friends, looking after your own people.

clue.text: Regular TUC outing in which one lands work?

indicators.note: in which says the next piece is placed inside
outing suggests a trip out, the letters going off in a new arrangement

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A regular trade-union day trip during which someone lands a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' shuffles REGULAR and TUC into AGRCULTURE, and I goes 'in which'. 'lands' looks like a verb but is the noun: work on the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming is the cultivation of land, so it is work on lands, with the question mark flagging the wordplay.

clue.text: Tablet swallowed — a pint's knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pill washed down with a pint drunk in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' looks like the drinking, but it holds the end letters; 'knocked back' turns DAPI around.
explanation.definitionFit: The iPad is Apple's well-known tablet computer.

clue.text: Sweet couple on vacation in America, going round topless

indicators.note: in puts the emptied couple inside the other letters
going round suggests the letters are spun into a new order
topless says the first letter of America is removed
on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters of couple are kept

explanation.surface: A sweet pair on holiday in the USA, travelling about without tops on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the first A from America, leaving MERICA; 'going round' shuffles it to ICREAM; 'on vacation' empties couple to CE, which goes 'in' after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen dessert, and a sweet is the British word for a dessert course.

clue.text: One getting stuck into sausages? That's right, after drinks

indicators.note: after puts the mark for right following the drinks

parts.note: cocktails are mixed drinks
a tick is the mark that says an answer is right

explanation.surface: A party guest digging into the sausages, rightly so, after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a greedy guest; it is a small wooden spike pushed into party sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail stick is a short pointed stick used to spear small party food such as sausages.

clue.text: Squid? After cooking, hope pal is into seafood

indicators.note: is into says the jumbled letters go inside the fish

parts.note: cod is a fish eaten as seafood

indicators.note: after cooking suggests the letters have been prepared and mixed

explanation.surface: Is this squid? Once cooked, someone hopes a friend likes seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows squid is only one example of the class. 'After cooking' sounds like kitchen talk but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid belong to the class of molluscs with arms attached to the head, along with octopus and cuttlefish.

clue.text: Free lunch includes fish

indicators.note: includes says the answer sits inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A free meal with fish on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snakelike fish.

clue.text: Dog almost had to metamorphose

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
to have a meal is to eat, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: A dog all but forced to transform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' clips MUTT to MUT; 'had' is the eating sense, ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate and to metamorphose both mean to change in form.

clue.text: Dish with two ingredients found in casino, one said

indicators.note: one said marks that only the first of the pair is to be taken as heard, a soundalike

parts.note: a stake is the money wagered at a casino
with means and, together
chips are the tokens gamblers use at a casino

explanation.surface: A meal made from two things that turn up in a gambling house, one of them spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two ingredients found in casino' are a stake and chips; 'one said' changes stake to its soundalike steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak and chips is a classic British pub meal of beef with fried potatoes.

clue.text: Leave after eating most of light dessert

indicators.note: eating says the word for leave swallows the next piece

parts.note: to leave is to part, depart

indicators.note: most of says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: light as in fair, pale-coloured

explanation.surface: Going off after finishing nearly all of a light pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the R from FAIR, leaving FAI, which PART is 'eating'. 'light dessert' looks like one phrase, but light belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A parfait is a layered frozen or chilled sweet course, so it is a kind of dessert.

clue.text: Baked apple, cored and cut for Juliet?

indicators.note: baked suggests the letters are cooked up and rearranged
cored says the central letter of apple is taken out

explanation.surface: A baked apple with the core removed, sliced up for a girl called Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cored' removes the middle P of apple, leaving APLE; with CUT that is shuffled by 'Baked'. The question mark flags Juliet as an example of a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, the heroine belongs to the house of Capulet, the rival family to the Montagues.

clue.text: In a jam, headless grub

indicators.note: headless says the first letter is cut off

parts.note: in a jam means stuck, trapped in a difficult spot

explanation.surface: A larva with no head trapped in a pot of jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes the S of STUCK. Grub looks like an insect larva but is the slang sense of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British school slang for food, especially sweets and snacks, as grub is slang for food.

clue.text: Karate perhaps hurt one gangster into biting

parts.note: to hurt or spoil is to mar

indicators.note: into says the next pieces go inside the word for biting

parts.note: biting as in sharp-tasting, tart
one is the Roman numeral I
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL

explanation.surface: Someone hurt as a gangster turns to biting, a fight perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Gangster as AL is the usual nod to Al Capone. I and AL go 'into' TART to make TIALART.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is one example of a fighting discipline from the East, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: A small cut consumed by daughter, it's solemnly declared

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
to sever is to cut
consumed food was eaten, ate

explanation.surface: A little slice eaten by a daughter, it is gravely stated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' looks like a container, but the pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to affirm or state something earnestly and with conviction.

clue.text: Decorative bits of stem ginger at last — and no bananas!

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild
at last means the final letter of ginger

explanation.surface: Pretty touches made of stem ginger, with no bananas in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit but is slang for crazy, shuffling STEM, R, AND and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Adornments are ornaments or trimmings added to decorate something.

clue.text: Poor decision, alas, eating starter dish that's cold

indicators.note: poor signals the letters are in bad shape and rearranged
starter means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A sigh over a bad choice: eating a starter that turns out to be cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' shuffles DECISION and ALAS into SALADNICOIS, and 'starter' of eating adds the final E. Starter looks like a course of the meal, adding to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Salade niçoise is a cold French salad of tuna, eggs, olives and beans, served from Nice.

clue.text: See 16
See 9
Alec's tea involved mushroom and rocket

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the apostrophe drops but the S counts here

explanation.surface: Alec's tea was made with mushroom and rocket leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushroom and rocket look like foods but are both verbs for growing fast; the S of Alec's is a fodder letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom and to rocket both mean to increase rapidly, as costs do when they rise sharply.

clue.text: I say! All the birds are devouring large round fruit cakes

indicators.note: say signals that what follows is how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
a round shape, a ring, looks like the letter O
Aves is the scientific class covering all birds

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a flock of birds devouring a big round fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say!' looks like an exclamation, but I is current, which spoken sounds like currant. 'are devouring' is loose: L and O sit in front of AVES rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Currant loaves are sweet breads studded with dried fruit, so they are fruit cakes in a broad sense.

clue.text: See 20
Line on chart showing duck served in island pub

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nought, O
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A weather chart showing duck on the menu in an island pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nought, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal air pressure.

clue.text: See 5
Waxy whale product: seamen reportedly serve it in a turnover

parts.note: seamen spoken sounds like semen, and semen is another word for sperm, so the pair gives that word
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

indicators.note: in a turnover says the little word it is flipped round to read backwards

explanation.surface: Sailors, so the story goes, serve up a wax from whales inside a pastry turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes seamen sound like semen, which means sperm. A tennis serve gives ACE, and 'in a turnover' flips IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Spermaceti is the white waxy substance found in the head of the sperm whale, once used for candles.

clue.text: Flower given a bit of water

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A bloom is given a little water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river, here the Ure in North Yorkshire, England. 'water' is the euphemism for urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a compound present in urine, and urine is politely called water, so it is one part of it.

clue.text: Yes, sailor served up a type of bean

indicators.note: served up in a down clue says the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for yes
OS is ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor says yes to a dish of beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses AYOS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The soya bean is a legume grown for oil, protein and tofu.

clue.text: Corrupt judge in Northern Ireland is a dog

parts.note: corrupt in the sense of base, morally low

indicators.note: in says the judge goes inside Northern Ireland's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A crooked judge in Northern Ireland is a dog, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Corrupt looks like a verb or an anagram signal but is the adjective base.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a barkless hunting breed originally from central Africa.

clue.text: Health resort a bit short of luncheon meat?

indicators.note: a bit short of says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Spam is the tinned luncheon meat

explanation.surface: A health resort slightly lacking in tinned meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a place with mineral springs or treatments visited for health.

clue.text: Country area goes after cultivation of mostly both oats and rice

indicators.note: goes after places the letter for area at the end
cultivation of says the letters that follow are worked over like soil, rearranged
mostly says the last letter of the word is dropped
both carries the trimming over to rice as well as oats

explanation.surface: A region comes after farming most of its oats and rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly both' trims oats to OAT and rice to RIC; 'cultivation of' shuffles them to CROATI, and A 'goes after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a nation on the Adriatic coast of the Balkans.

clue.text: Some immature asses slander judge again

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few childish fools badmouth someone and then think again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate or appraise something a second time.

clue.text: Cut of meat, second to go off

parts.note: eggs that addle go off, turn rotten

explanation.surface: A joint of meat, with a second one about to turn bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle of lamb or venison is the joint from both loins with the backbone.
